hints.S51_A1: The wings are compared to PAPER, and SUNLIGHT SHONE RIGHT THROUGH them. Ask: can light pass through something heavy, thick or dark? Match the adjective to the paper, not to the pond.
hints.S51_A2: The specimen is RARE and must NOT BE DAMAGED, so the scientist wants to keep it safe. Ask: which phrasal verb means to take care of something? 'Destroy', 'ignore' and 'hide' would all put the beetle at risk.
hints.S51_A3: It began as a DULL BROWN CATERPILLAR and ended with DAZZLING ORANGE AND BLACK WINGS - a complete change of body. Ask: which verb means to change completely into something new? 'Escaped' only tells you where it went.
hints.S51_A4: The light is GENTLE and compared to a TINY DANCING STAR - it keeps blinking, rather than dying away. Ask: which verb shows an unsteady, wavering light? 'Faded', 'disappeared' and 'shrank' all mean it is going away.
hints.S51_A5: A single COLONY holds MILLIONS OF INDIVIDUALS ALL WORKING TOGETHER. Ask: does that describe an insect that lives alone, or one that lives in an organised group? 'Solitary' says the exact opposite.
hints.S51_B1: Cover the words IN THE SCIENCE CLASS and look at what is left: NOBODY. That one word is the subject, and it counts as a single person. Ask: which present-tense ending does a singular subject demand?
hints.S51_B2: SINCE LAST YEAR tells you the garden was made in the past and is still there, and HAS is already in place. Ask: which of the four forms can follow 'has' to build a present perfect?
hints.S51_B3: THAN is sitting in the sentence, so two distances are being measured against each other. Ask: does a comparison take the plain adjective, the -est form, or the -er form? 'Very' can never sit in front of a comparative.
hints.S51_B4: The butterfly SUDDENLY FLEW OUT OF THE NET - a short, sharp event cutting across a longer one. Ask: which choice shows the students already in the middle of watching it? A plain past verb reports only a finished action.
hints.S51_B5: INFORMATION is a word you cannot count - never 'one information, two informations'. Ask: which quantity word goes with an uncountable noun? 'A few', 'many' and 'several' all need things you can count one by one.
hints.S51_B6: Find the verb of the main clause: the display WAS the most beautiful thing. The tag copies THAT verb, not the 'have' hidden inside 'you have ever seen'. Ask: after a positive statement, is the tag positive or negative?
hints.S51_B7: The specimen did not act - somebody FOUND it IN THE JUNGLE and moved it TO THE NATIONAL MUSEUM. Ask: which choice makes the subject the receiver of the action, and sets it in the past?
hints.S51_B8: This is a reported command with a warning: OR IT MIGHT STRIKE AT THEIR FINGERS. Ask: after 'told + person', which form follows - the plain verb, the -ing form, or 'to' + verb? And where does the negative word sit?
hints.S51_C1: The blank opens the sentence and DOES the spotting of the MANTIS on the wall. Ask: does a subject pronoun or an object pronoun belong here? The writer is the one telling the story, so pick the first-person subject form.
hints.S51_C2: The verb ASKED comes first, and the blank RECEIVES the asking - the teacher does the action, not the writer. Ask: after a verb, do we use the subject form or the object form of the first-person pronoun?
hints.S51_C3: DION is a boy, and the blank DOES the knowing - 'knows the name of every bug'. Ask: which pronoun can stand as the subject of a sentence, and which one can only follow a verb? Subject form, single male.
hints.S51_C4: 'ASK' is the verb and the blank comes straight after it, so the blank receives the asking. Ask: which male pronoun follows a verb - the one that opens a sentence, or the object form? A subject pronoun never sits after a verb.
hints.S51_C5: The science teacher is female, and the blank DOES the keeping - 'ONCE KEPT a pet stick insect'. Ask: does the subject slot take the acting form or the receiving form? Pick the female form that can open a sentence.
hints.S51_C6: The verb SURPRISED sits right in front of the blank, and the one who got the surprise is the female teacher. Ask: after a verb, do we use the form that acts, or the form that receives? Female plus object slot.
hints.S51_C7: ANTS is plural, and the blank DOES the carrying - 'can carry fifty times their weight'. Ask: which plural pronoun is able to be the subject of a sentence? The other plural form can only follow a verb.
hints.S51_C8: SCIENTISTS do the studying, and the ants RECEIVE it. Ask: after the verb STUDIED, does the plural subject form or the plural object form belong here? A subject pronoun can never sit after a verb.
hints.S51_D1: The next sentence proves it: the STICK INSECT LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE A TWIG. Ask: which box word names the trick of blending into the background? 'Antennae' are feelers and 'larvae' are young - neither is a way of hiding.
hints.S51_D2: The sentence defines itself: AN ANIMAL THAT HUNTS AND EATS OTHER ANIMALS. Ask: which box word names the hunter rather than the hunted? A 'habitat' is a place, not a creature.
hints.S51_D3: The dashes explain it: THE LONG FEELERS ON THEIR HEADS, used to SENSE VIBRATIONS. Ask: which box word names those feelers? An insect has two of them, so the word must be plural.
hints.S51_D4: The clue is WORM-LIKE YOUNG THAT HATCH FROM EGGS - the stage that comes before the adult insect. Ask: which box word names the young of insects? A caterpillar is exactly this stage of a butterfly.
hints.S51_D5: A HEALTHY GARDEN is a place, and the blank comes after 'the ideal'. Ask: which box word names the natural home where a creature feeds, breeds and shelters? 'Camouflage' is a trick, not a place.
hints.S51_E1: Find the subject of the underlined verb: THE BUTTERFLIES - more than one. Ask: does a plural subject take the singular past form of 'to be', or the plural one? Never choose the verb by the word nearest to it.
hints.S51_E2: The underlined word as written means 'belonging to it', but the sentence is saying HARD TO BELIEVE. Ask: can you stretch it into the two words 'it is' and still make sense? If yes, an apostrophe is missing.
hints.S51_E3: The underlined word sits in front of WORKER, and its two vowels are the wrong way round. Ask: with no C in front, does the I lead or does the E lead? Compare: field, brief, believe.
hints.S51_E4: MOVED is an action verb, and the underlined word tells you HOW the caterpillar moved ALONG THE BRANCH. Ask: after a verb, do we use an adjective or an adverb? Manner words nearly always take the -ly ending.
hints.S51_E5: The NOTES AND PHOTOGRAPHS belong to the whole class - the owners are many, not one. Ask: which mark shows ownership, and does it come before or after the -s when the plural already ends in -s?
hints.S51_F1: 'AS LONG AS' sets the condition, so it goes in front of the sentence about REMOVING FALLEN LEAVES. Ask: after a condition word, do we use a present verb or 'will'? And where must the comma go?
hints.S51_F2: 'SINCE' introduces the background reason, so start with the sentence about the CHEMICAL REACTION. Ask: which fact explains the other? In the second half, a pronoun replaces the repeated FIREFLY.
